procedure.description: panniculectomy with excision of excess skin and subcutaneous tissue of the abdomen

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Lanternhill Health Plan denied the claim for CPT 15847 (panniculectomy with excision of excess skin and subcutaneous tissue of the abdomen) with date of service 2026-08-08. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: The documentation does not establish a functional impairment or failure of conservative treatment of the skin condition.

criteria.text: Panniculus hangs at or below the level of the pubis (grade 2 or higher) as documented on examination.

Recurrent or chronic intertrigo, cellulitis, or skin breakdown beneath the panniculus that has failed at least 3 months of conservative treatment such as topical antifungals, hygiene measures, and barrier products.
Weight stable within 10 pounds for at least 12 months (or at least 18 months after bariatric surgery).
The panniculus interferes with activities of daily living or ambulation.

chart.text: Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

38 year old woman here about the abdominal apron after her weight loss. Nice result on the weight. Discussed panniculectomy versus a full abdominoplasty and what insurance will and will not look at. Her history otherwise: migraines, rare now, prediabetes, diet controlled. Allergies: penicillin, rash. Never smoked, occasional beer, has three kids at home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. On exam the pannus hangs well below the pubis, I would call it grade 2, with maceration and an odor in the fold. She has been fighting the rash under the apron for better than a year, treated with nystatin, then clotrimazole, keeps it dry with powder and a cloth liner, and it comes right back. Two rounds of antibiotics from the PCP for cellulitis in the fold. Down 126 pounds after the sleeve in 2024. Weight has been steady at 179 give or take five for the last 20 months. Says she cannot walk more than a block without the skin fold chafing raw, has to lift it to wash underneath, cannot find pants that fit over it.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Follow-up on the abdomen. Went back over the operation, drains, the scar, recovery of four to six weeks. She understands this is skin and fat removal for the skin problems, not a tummy tuck. Vitals today 135 over 86, pulse 64. Rash is back again despite 6 months of the antifungal and barrier routine. Fold is red and weeping today. Weight 177 today, holding.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.
Blood pressure check. 135 over 72 today, 135 over 84 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 205, LDL 114, HDL 55, triglycerides 103. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
She called asking where things stand with the insurance. Told her the paperwork went in and we are waiting to hear. Reviewed what to do in the meantime.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Here with a cough and congestion for 7 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 16 and 14. No ocular pathology noted.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, she remains sure about going ahead.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 2 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Pre-op. Consent signed. Marked the resection with her standing. Nicotine negative. Hold the metformin the morning of.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
